claim_text: The biomarker review in this packet emphasizes that, among many proposed markers including PTEN loss, AKT signaling, insulin levels, FDG-PET response, FGFR alterations, KRAS, and TP53, only PIK3CA mutation had established predictive value for alpha-selective or beta-sparing PI3K inhibitors in the advanced breast cancer setting at the time of review, while many other signals were retrospective, exploratory, or assay-dependent `pmid-31859350`.
evidence_summary: Annals of Oncology review explicitly analyzes PIK3CA mutations, PI3K pathway activation, PTEN loss, Akt signaling, insulin levels, FDG-PET, FGFR1/2 amplification, KRAS, and TP53, and concludes that most data are retrospective or exploratory while only PIK3CA had proven predictive value for alpha-selective alpelisib and beta-sparing taselisib at publication. Limitation is review-level and time-dependent evidence.
reviewer_notes: Supported by the review abstract and biomarker synthesis.

claim_text: Comprehensive genomic profiling refines the eligibility layer: in a large tissue and liquid biopsy analysis, 20 percent of PIK3CA-mutant breast cancer samples carried pathogenic mutations outside the original SOLAR-1 hotspot set, and patients with those other mutations had longer real-world PFS on alpelisib plus fulvestrant than on fulvestrant alone, supporting broader mutation detection while preserving uncertainty about variant-specific benefit `pmid-36321996`.
evidence_summary: Large comprehensive genomic profiling study analyzed tens of thousands of tissue biopsies, liquid biopsies, and a clinico-genomic HR-positive HER2-negative advanced breast cancer cohort; it reported that mutations outside the approved SOLAR-1 substitutions represented about 20 percent of PIK3CA-mutant breast cancers and that OTHERm patients had longer real-world PFS with alpelisib plus fulvestrant than fulvestrant alone. Limitation is retrospective real-world analysis and variant-specific uncertainty.
reviewer_notes: Supported; corrected prose should preserve the retrospective nature of the rwPFS comparison.

claim_text: Those observations support PTEN loss as a PI3Kalpha resistance marker and ESR1 as endocrine-partner escape in the same regimen, rather than treating both as equivalent PI3Kalpha biomarkers `pmid-32864625`.
evidence_summary: Alpelisib plus aromatase inhibitor translational study found PTEN loss-of-function alterations at baseline or post-treatment in resistant patients and expansion of ESR1 activating mutations during therapy; ESR1 modeling showed faster progression on alpelisib plus estrogen deprivation, supporting endocrine-component escape distinct from PTEN-mediated PI3Kalpha resistance. Limitation is small phase I/II cohort without aromatase-inhibitor-only comparator.
reviewer_notes: Supported and appropriately distinguishes biomarker function.

claim_text: Functional modeling further split therapeutic implications, because some PIK3CA resistance mutations were sensitive to allosteric PI3Kalpha inhibition whereas co-emergent AKT1 alterations required AKT-directed logic `pmid-37916958`.
evidence_summary: Acquired-resistance study used serial ctDNA, autopsy profiling, structural modeling, and engineered breast cancer cells to show secondary PIK3CA mutations reduced orthosteric inhibitor activity but retained sensitivity to allosteric RLY-2608, while AKT1 mutant models were resistant to orthosteric and allosteric PI3Kalpha inhibition and remained sensitive to AKT inhibitors. Limitation is model-guided therapeutic inference in advanced breast cancer.
reviewer_notes: Supported by the abstract, introduction, and functional sections.

claim_text: Functional screens and perturbation models can nominate actionable mechanisms, such as PIM kinase upregulation maintaining downstream PI3K effector activity after BYL719, but the paired patient-biopsy support was small and preliminary `pmid-27604488`.
evidence_summary: BYL719 gain-of-function screen in breast cancer cells identified and validated PIM kinases as resistance genes that maintained PRAS40/BAD and downstream effector signaling, with PI3K plus PIM inhibition overcoming resistance; paired biopsy RNA analyses showed some validated genes increased after relapse but were explicitly limited by small preliminary clinical sampling. Limitation is stronger functional than clinical biomarker evidence.

claim_text: Similarly, FGFR1 overexpression in luminal MCF-7 and T47D cells conferred alpelisib resistance with sustained Akt, ERK, S6K, Rb, and ER-alpha phosphorylation, and FGFR1 knockdown or AZD4547 combinations restored sensitivity in vitro; this is strong perturbation/rescue evidence, not yet a validated clinical selection rule `pmid-40510030`.
evidence_summary: Luminal breast cancer cell-line study used isogenic MCF-7 and T47D FGFR1-overexpressing models, viability, colony, cell-cycle, Western blot, siRNA knockdown, and combination-index assays; FGFR1 increased alpelisib resistance with sustained p-Akt, p-Erk, p-S6K, p-Rb, and ER-alpha phosphorylation, while FGFR1 knockdown or AZD4547 combinations restored sensitivity. Limitation is in vitro only with no patient outcome validation.
reviewer_notes: Supported; the limitation clause is important and should be retained.

claim_text: Action distinguishes eligibility for alpelisib or inavolisib, switching endocrine therapy for ESR1-mutant disease, considering AKT-pathway targeting for PTEN or AKT1 alterations, testing PI3Kalpha inhibitor class switching for secondary PIK3CA mutations, and treating FGFR or other RTK markers as investigational combination hypotheses `pmid-39935426` `pmid-42351448` `pmid-42445743` `pmid-32817061`.
corrected_claim: Action distinguishes eligibility for approved PI3Kalpha-directed regimens, endocrine therapy selection for ESR1-mutant disease, AKT-pathway targeting for PTEN or AKT1 alterations, and treating FGFR or other RTK markers as investigational hypotheses.
evidence_summary: The cited clinical perspective and narrative reviews support biomarker-guided categories for PIK3CA eligibility, ESR1-directed endocrine switching, PI3K/AKT/PTEN pathway targeting, and investigational FGFR/RTK hypotheses after endocrine or CDK4/6 resistance. However, these cited papers do not provide the primary acquired-resistance evidence for testing PI3Kalpha inhibitor class switching specifically for secondary PIK3CA mutations; that point would require the separate acquired-resistance citation. Limitations are review-level synthesis and guideline-date dependence.
reviewer_notes: Partially supported because one action category is undercited/mismatched to the listed papers.
